html:
Iceland is a volcanic island in the North Atlantic, just south of the Arctic Circle. On the map from 1880 it belongs first to Denmark, then stands as its own state.

Norse settlers, many from Norway, settled the island from about 874. They ruled themselves without a king in the Icelandic Commonwealth, with law made at the Althing, an open air assembly founded in 930. In the year 1000 the Althing accepted Christianity by agreement. The sagas written in the 1200s record this world.

In 1262 Iceland submitted to the king of Norway, and through the Kalmar Union it passed to Denmark. For centuries it was poor, cut off and hit by eruptions and famine; Danish merchants held a trade monopoly until 1787.

In the 1800s a national movement led by Jón Sigurðsson won a constitution in 1874 and home rule in 1904. In 1918 Iceland became a separate kingdom sharing the Danish king. During the Second World War Britain and then the United States occupied it, and in 1944 Iceland declared itself a republic. It joined NATO in 1949 without an army. Fish was its wealth, and it fought the Cod Wars with Britain over fishing limits. Its banks collapsed in the crisis of 2008.
sum: Iceland is a volcanic island in the North Atlantic, just south of the Arctic Circle. On the map from 1880 it belongs first to Denmark, then stands as its own state.
